subject: Staggered provisioning & GPU-cost sensitivity — approval request for reserved commit
messages:
From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 25 Sep 2026 09:32:00 -0700
Subject: Staggered provisioning & GPU-cost sensitivity — approval request for reserved commit

Hi team,

Following up on today's call with Nebula Labs (Claire & procurement), they want to move forward with a reserved capacity commit but are asking for two concessions tied to current GPU market volatility: a staged provisioning schedule (phased activation across Q1–Q3 2027) and a GPU-price-sensitivity discount clause that would trigger a capped credit if on-market spot/sku costs exceed a threshold.

Key ask from sales/AE: we need a written approval (or clear escalation path) for:
- A 24-month commit at a 30% list discount with a staged activation (50% pool on day 1, 25% at month 6, final 25% at month 12).
- A GPU-cost-sensitivity credit: if the aggregate fleet GPU index moves > 18% vs. the baseline we used for pricing, Nebula gets a 6% credit on months where the index exceeds that threshold.

Sizing / justification (attached nebula-sizing-sheet-v3.xlsx):
- Initial pool: 48 A100-equivalent concurrent slots (peak concurrency) to support their expected Q1 burst patterns.
- Average utilization ramp expected 30% -> 65% over the first 9 months.

Operational notes: the staged activation reduces upfront capital commitment and helps us preserve flexibility in GPU allocation. We can enable rollback (pause activation of the later tranche) if utilization deviates by >40% from forecast for two consecutive months.

Risks/finance implications: this structure exposes Redwood to short-term price movement on our procurement side; finance needs to confirm whether the credit can be paid as a rebate vs. a billing credit and confirm P&L treatment.

Request: Kimberly / Marcus — can you sign off on the discount level and the credit trigger (or propose an alternate threshold/credit)? If not approvable, please propose the escalation path and exact approver(s).

Cc'ing Grace for ops impact and sequencing. I included the draft redline (proposed-commit-term-redline.pdf).

Thanks,

--
Mateo Alvarez
Account Executive, Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
+1 (415) 555-0172

Attachments: nebula-sizing-sheet-v3.xlsx (spreadsheet), proposed-commit-term-redline.pdf (redline PDF)

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>

Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 25 Sep 2026 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Staggered provisioning & GPU-cost sensitivity — approval request for reserved commit

Mateo — thanks for the clear breakdown and attachments. A few quick questions from pricing/finance side: 

1) Baseline definition: what date range / procurement basket did we use to compute the baseline GPU index? Need to know whether the baseline is pre- or post-Q2 procurement spikes.
2) Credit mechanics: is Nebula expecting an automatic month-over-month credit or a reconciliation credit at the end of each quarter? Ops prefers a reconciliation to avoid monthly adjustments in billing.
3) Risk cap: can we cap the total lifetime credit (e.g., 6% credit capped at 8% of total committed invoice)? Finance prefers a capped exposure rather than an open-ended monthly credit.

Initial thought: 30% list discount is in range but the 6% monthly credit trigger with no cap is risky. If we define the baseline as the trailing-3-month weighted procurement basket and do a quarterly reconciliation with a lifetime cap at 7% of committed revenue, I think this is workable. Also need Marcus to confirm whether staged activation requires any special reservation mechanics on our side (phased GPU reservations vs. single allocation with throttling).

Can you confirm Nebula is okay with quarterly reconciliation and a lifetime cap? If they push monthly credits we should push back.

-Kim

--
Kimberly Park
Head of Pricing, Revenue Ops
Redwood Inference

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 28 Sep 2026 14:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Staggered provisioning & GPU-cost sensitivity — approval request for reserved commit

Kim / Mateo — digging into the ops and capacity side. Short answers below, longer ops notes attached inline.

- Baseline: ops suggests using a weighted basket: recent committed-price average (May–Jul 2026) weighted by SKU mix; that avoids anchoring to an outlier month. I agree with a quarterly reconciliation approach.

- Staged activation: we can implement provisioning as three tranches. Implementation options: 
  * Option A: create three separate reserved pools (preferred for visibility and billing isolation).
  * Option B: create one bucket with activation flags (simpler for the customer, harder for internal capacity tracking).

Impact on internal scheduling: Option A requires reserving capacity in our scheduler ahead of activation windows; that increases our short-term allocation pressure but provides clearer reclaim/rollback mechanics. Option B gives us flexibility but makes forecasting/ops accounting fuzzier.

- Credit exposure: from an ops perspective the credit is independent of capacity allocation; it's purely financial. Recommend a lifetime cap (Kim suggested 7% — acceptable). Also suggest a minimum utilization guard: credit only applies if Nebula's paid utilization across tranches > 40% over the reconciliation quarter (prevents gaming by purchasing capacity but not using it).

I'll attach a quick ops checklist in the drive link below (added to related_links). If we go with Option A (three pools) finance needs to know the reservation dates so they can match to procurement hedges.

-Marcus

--
Marcus Lin
Director, Dedicated Capacity Operations
Redwood Inference

From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Claire Johnson <claire@nebula.ai>, procurement@nebula.ai
Date: Mon, 27 Sep 2026 15:45:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Staggered provisioning & GPU-cost sensitivity — approval request for reserved commit

Thanks all — looping Claire so Nebula sees our proposed guardrails. Per our internal alignment: 

- Pricing team (Kim) and Ops (Marcus) propose: quarterly reconciliation, baseline = weighted May–Jul 2026 procurement basket, lifetime credit cap = 7% of committed invoice, and credit only applies if paid utilization > 40% in the reconciliation quarter.
- Activation mechanics: prefer Option A (three separate reserved pools) with explicit activation dates: 2027-01-03, 2027-07-01, 2028-01-02. Activation windows can shift +/- 14 days for calendar reasons.
- Contract redline: we accept the 24-month term at 30% list discount if the above guardrails are added. Also require a mutual rollback clause: if our procurement index goes up AND Nebula's utilization is < 40% for two consecutive quarters, we reserve the right to pause the next tranche activation (with 30 days' notice).

Claire — please confirm Nebula accepts the quarterly reconciliation and capped-credit approach. If you prefer monthly reconciliations instead of quarterly, call me and we'll discuss internal tradeoffs.

Regards,

Grace O'Connor
Senior Manager, Dedicated Customer Success
Redwood Inference
